title: The count and the goal
hook: A toy dashboard counts more items by adding unusable ones. What happens to usable share?

knows: basic arithmetic and the meaning of a percentage
doesNotKnow: Inspect whether an output metric preserves the named quality objective after the counted activity increases.

misconception: Raising an activity count necessarily raises progress toward the stated quality goal.

claims.text: Original stipulated selection model: A inputs [10, 100, 0, 0] yield 100; B inputs [10, 100, 10, 0] yield 50. Prediction correct option 50. A shows {A}%; B shows {B}%. The count doubles from ten to twenty, but usable outputs remain ten and their fraction halves. Usability is a stipulated binary score; no organizational incentive effect is inferred.

claims.text: A toy process produces 12 usable and 8 unusable items. What percentage is usable? 12 of 20 items are usable: 60%. Counting all twenty alone does not express that quality goal.
